findings.description: The MySQL parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = ON (or otherwise enforce SSL/TLS), so the catalog database will accept unencrypted client connections, allowing credentials and catalog data to travel in cleartext between the app server and RDS.

The instance user_data interpolates the RDS master username and the password variable (var.password) directly into a bash heredoc that writes /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is stored unencrypted and is retrievable by anyone with instance metadata access (including via SSRF from the web app) or ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking the database master credentials.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. Combined with an attached IAM instance profile (aws_iam_instance_profile.catalog_app_profile) and a PHP application that processes untrusted POST input, a server-side request forgery would allow theft of the role's temporary credentials.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so the EBS root volume (which stores the database credentials written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc) may be unencrypted at rest unless account-level EBS default encryption is in force.

The bootstrap script installs and starts httpd serving the credential-handling PHP page over plain HTTP only, with no TLS configuration or redirect, so form submissions containing personal data and session traffic traverse the network in cleartext.

The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the catalog database's stored data, snapshots, and logs are written unencrypted. Any compromise of underlying storage or snapshot sharing exposes data in cleartext.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, exposing the database to internet-based attack (credential stuffing, exploitation of MySQL) rather than confining it to the VPC.

The master password is supplied via var.password and the username is the predictable static value 'admin'; the credential is stored in Terraform state/variable files in cleartext instead of being generated and stored in Secrets Manager (manage_master_user_password).

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the EC2 catalog app server. This violates least privilege and provides a direct privilege-escalation/lateral-movement path (e.g. reading any S3 bucket, modifying security groups, or snapshotting/restoring any RDS instance) if the publicly reachable instance is compromised.

The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, which permits data exfiltration and command-and-control callbacks from a compromised database host with no network boundary.

Port 3306 is open to the entire VPC CIDR rather than restricted to the application server's security group, allowing any workload in the VPC to reach the database directly. Combined with publicly_accessible = true on the instance, this ingress rule is the only remaining control on exposure.

No enforcement of TLS for client connections is configured (e.g. require_secure_transport in the parameter group is not set here), so MySQL clients may connect over cleartext to an internet-facing endpoint.
